Beneath it two runs, Monday and Thursday, each write a glossary and decision records beside the skill. A current carries Monday's files into Thursday's run, and Thursday's glossary is one term longer: Core.

project-context-written-beside-the-skill.header: Project context written beside the skill, read next run
project-context-written-beside-the-skill.description: Anthropic says models, like people who use "file systems, inboxes, and bookmarks", do well with notes kept outside the context window [1], and a skill should teach an approach while reading instance details from files [2]. The grill-with-docs files are this repository's own copy of Matt Pocock's skill [3], not a research source. The Slide shows grill-with-docs only; the grill-me skill is not shown.

the-interview-is-the-card.title: The interview is the card
the-interview-is-the-card.script: Let me show you inside and beside together, on real files instead of the dive. This is grill-with-docs, a skill by Matt Pocock that I use, and it runs an interview, which is the procedure. It stays the same every time.

follow-the-arrow.title: Follow the arrow
follow-the-arrow.script: While it runs, grill-with-docs writes files beside itself, a glossary and decision records, and the next run checks your words against them. The skill stays the same, and what it learned about your project waits beside it.

skills-can-run-skills.title: Skills can run skills
skills-can-run-skills.script: One last thing: a skill can also run other skills: grill-with-docs runs one called grilling and another called domain-modeling. There is no settled name for that yet, and I'll leave it there.
